annotations.title: Write a month of video ideas

description: Start a content calendar for a topic, for "start a faceless account" or "a month of posts about X": count faceless videos (1-31) over days (7-31), each with a title, hook, the exact script, caption, hashtags and a posting time. Best: write the ideas yourself and send them as items (taken as written, at once); otherwise Clypmint writes them (the call waits until they are written, or says to call again with the same operation_id). Makes nothing and spends nothing: answers plan_id, the ideas and the quote (credits a video, room left this month). Show the user the ideas and change them with edit_content_plan. After their yes, make them with create_videos (10 a call). Cost: Free to write; making each video costs about 4 credits (30 s).

count.description: How many videos (1-31); leave out when sending items.

instructions.description: Anything else about the calendar, in the user's words.

items.description: Ideas you wrote yourself (title, hook, script, caption, hashtags): taken as written, at once. Without them Clypmint writes the ideas.
One word, letters, digits or _, with or without #.

script.description: The exact words the narrator reads, about 2.5 words a second of video.

operation_id.description: The same id on a retry runs it once; a new id is a new request.

platforms.description: Where each post goes; Instagram when left out.

seconds.description: How long each video is: 15, 30 or 60 seconds.

start_at.description: The first day; tomorrow when left out.

style_id.description: A style id from browse_styles for every video.

timezone.description: The IANA time zone of the posting times, e.g. America/Chicago.

voice.description: The narrator for a video made from words (sarah: calm, health and money; alice: clear British educator; brian: deep documentary; liam: energetic ads; browse_styles describes all 21). Left out: the style's own narrator, or one that fits the words.

name: plan_content

outputSchema.description: Clypmint plan_content result. Error results carry error; successful requests expose the identifiers and state available for the next step. Signed media stays in private metadata.
